questions.stem: Which is the ONLY liquid metal at room temperature (25°C)?
questions.explanation: MERCURY (Hg, atomic number 80) is the ONLY metal liquid at standard room temperature (~25°C). Melting point: −38.83°C. Also called 'quicksilver'. Used in thermometers, barometers, fluorescent lamps — but toxic, so being phased out (Minamata Convention 2013). GALLIUM (Ga, mp 29.76°C) — melts in your warm hand but SOLID at 25°C. CESIUM (mp 28.44°C) and RUBIDIUM (mp 39.31°C) also melt just above room temp but are SOLID at 25°C — and they're highly reactive alkali metals. FRANCIUM (mp ~27°C estimated; highly radioactive). Among NON-METALS, BROMINE is the only element liquid at room temp (mp −7°C). So the other LIQUID element at RT is BROMINE (non-metal).

questions.explanation: Key alloys with compositions: BRASS = Cu (~70%) + Zn (~30%). BRONZE = Cu + Sn (tin) — the oldest alloy (Bronze Age ~3300 BCE). STEEL = Fe + C (< 2%). STAINLESS STEEL = Fe + Cr (11%+) + Ni. CAST IRON = Fe + C (2-4%). WROUGHT IRON = Fe + C (<0.2%). SOLDER = Pb + Sn (historically). PEWTER = Sn + Sb + Cu. DURALUMIN = Al + Cu + Mg + Mn (aircraft). MAGNALIUM = Al + Mg (light). NICHROME = Ni + Cr + Fe (heating elements). GERMAN SILVER (despite name, no silver) = Cu + Ni + Zn. MONEL = Ni + Cu. AMALGAM = any metal + Hg (dental fillings: Hg + Ag + Sn + Cu). WHITE GOLD = Au + Pd or Au + Ni. ROSE GOLD = Au + Cu.

questions.stem: Which metal is extracted from the ore BAUXITE?
questions.explanation: Metal-ore mapping: ALUMINIUM from BAUXITE (Al₂O₃·2H₂O) via Hall-Héroult electrolysis after Bayer process refining. IRON from HAEMATITE (Fe₂O₃, 70% Fe — main ore), MAGNETITE (Fe₃O₄), LIMONITE, SIDERITE (FeCO₃) — extracted in BLAST FURNACE. COPPER from CHALCOPYRITE (CuFeS₂ — main), COPPER PYRITES, MALACHITE (green Cu carbonate), AZURITE. ZINC from SPHALERITE / ZINC BLENDE (ZnS), CALAMINE (ZnCO₃), ZINCITE (ZnO). LEAD from GALENA (PbS). MERCURY from CINNABAR (HgS). TIN from CASSITERITE (SnO₂). SILVER from ARGENTITE (Ag₂S) + byproduct of Pb extraction. GOLD: native, in quartz veins. MAGNESIUM from DOLOMITE (MgCO₃·CaCO₃), MAGNESITE, seawater. URANIUM from PITCHBLENDE / URANINITE (UO₂), MONAZITE (also Th).

questions.stem: Galvanisation is a process in which iron is coated with which metal to prevent rusting?
questions.explanation: GALVANISATION = coating iron with ZINC to prevent rusting. Zinc is more reactive than iron — acts as SACRIFICIAL PROTECTION (even if the zinc layer scratches, Zn corrodes preferentially). Hot-dip (most common) or electroplating. Used for GI sheets, pipes, nails, water tanks. TINNING = iron coated with TIN (less reactive, forms barrier; used for food cans — tin doesn't react with most foods). Comparison corrosion protection methods: (1) GALVANISATION (Zn coat); (2) TINNING (Sn coat); (3) PAINTING / ENAMELLING; (4) ELECTROPLATING (Cu, Cr, Ni); (5) ALLOYING (stainless steel = Fe + Cr); (6) CATHODIC PROTECTION with a more reactive sacrificial anode (Mg bars on ship hulls).

questions.stem: Which metal has the HIGHEST electrical conductivity at room temperature?
questions.explanation: Electrical conductivity (highest to lower among common metals): SILVER (Ag — highest), COPPER (Cu — 2nd, widely used due to lower cost), GOLD (Au — 3rd, used in fine electronics for corrosion resistance), ALUMINIUM (Al — lighter, used in overhead power lines), TUNGSTEN, ZINC, NICKEL. Heat conductivity has a similar order (Wiedemann-Franz law). Diamond (non-metal) actually has the highest THERMAL conductivity, but is an electrical INSULATOR. Among metals, silver is also the most REFLECTIVE (mirrors historically used silver backing). Superconductors (like Hg below 4.2K, YBa2Cu3O7 above 77K 'high-Tc') have ZERO electrical resistance below critical temp.

questions.stem: Stainless steel is primarily an alloy of iron with which two other metals?
questions.explanation: STAINLESS STEEL = Fe + Chromium (≥ 10.5%) + Nickel (often 8%+) + small C. The chromium forms a passive Cr₂O₃ layer that prevents rusting — this is the 'stainless' property. Discovered 1913 by Harry Brearley (Sheffield, UK). Grades: 304 (18-8 — most common, 18% Cr 8% Ni), 316 (adds Mo for marine corrosion), 410 (cutlery). Mo is sometimes added for acid resistance. Nichrome = Ni + Cr + Fe (heating coils). Invar = Fe + Ni (36% Ni — low thermal expansion, used in precision instruments). Kovar = Fe + Ni + Co (matches borosilicate glass expansion).

questions.stem: The process of heating an ore in the presence of EXCESS AIR to convert it into an oxide is called:
questions.explanation: Metallurgy steps: (1) CRUSHING & GRINDING; (2) CONCENTRATION (froth flotation for sulphides, gravity separation, magnetic separation, leaching); (3) CONVERSION TO OXIDE: • ROASTING = heat in presence of EXCESS AIR (sulphide ores → oxides; e.g., 2ZnS + 3O₂ → 2ZnO + 2SO₂); • CALCINATION = heat in LIMITED / absence of air (carbonate/hydrate ores → oxides; e.g., ZnCO₃ → ZnO + CO₂ or CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂ or Al₂O₃·xH₂O → Al₂O₃ + H₂O); (4) REDUCTION: • SMELTING (carbon reduction in blast furnace — for Fe, Cu, Zn, Pb); • ALUMINOTHERMIC (for Mn, Cr); • ELECTROLYSIS (for reactive metals — Al, Mg, Na); (5) REFINING (liquation, poling, electrolytic — Cu, Zn, Al, Ag, Au).
